title: A 1.2-Million-Pound Monster Train Is Rolling Across America!
summary: Have you ever seen something so huge it makes your jaw drop? That’s what happened when the Big Boy No. 4014—the world’s largest working steam locomotive—rolled into Philadelphia. This 133-foot-long, 1.2-million-pound beast is on a coast-to-coast tour to celebrate America’s 250th birthday. On the hottest day of the year (102 degrees!), dozens of fans camped out at Valley Forge National Historical Park just to see it steam by. John Seibert, who came with his model railroad club, called it “a once-in-a-lifetime experience.” From miles away, you could hear the whistle. Then the headlights appeared, and the train thundered past, bells ringing and steam whistle blaring. “When he blew the whistle right by us, it kind of went right through you,” Seibert said. A few days later, the train parked in Philadelphia’s Navy Yard so crowds could get up close. Fifteen-year-old Brandon Westerfield said, “It’s so cool to see just something that big right in front of you.” His mom, who thought it was just another train, was amazed: “This is absolutely incredible.” The Big Boy was built in the 1940s to haul freight through mountains. Only eight were saved, and just one—No. 4014—still runs. Engineer Ed Dickens, who helped restore it, says everything is manually operated—no computers! So if you get a chance, go see this living piece of history. Just listen for that whistle.
why_it_matters: This living piece of history shows how people moved goods long before airplanes and trucks—a giant moving museum that reminds us how engineering helped build the country.

background_read: Steam trains once powered America, but they were replaced by diesel and electric engines long ago. The Big Boy was built to pull heavy freight trains over the Rocky Mountains.

Valley Forge National Historical Park is famous as the place where George Washington's army survived a harsh winter during the Revolutionary War. The train’s tour is part of America250, a nationwide celebration of the country's 250th birthday.
Article_Structure: WHO: The Big Boy No. 4014 steam locomotive, engineer Ed Dickens, and fans like John Seibert.
WHAT: A giant 133-foot-long steam train travels across America to celebrate the nation’s 250th birthday.
WHERE: Coast-to-coast, with stops including Valley Forge National Historical Park and the Philadelphia Navy Yard.
WHY: To let people experience a living piece of railroad history and marvel at a rare working steam locomotive.
